title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers a request of the provisioner contract with, application/json, as the integration contract's refusal, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/refusal.schema.json. The codes the starter meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking, for each cause that refusal lists, a replay under the replay rule of https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json among them: it tells the starter nothing about which cause applied, and the starter never takes it as the pool's access key being revoked; 403 forbidden, a request outside the key's rights, a claim whose pool_id is not the key's node pool, and a request naming a dispatch_id that is unknown or of another node pool than the key's, each with the same signed body as an unknown id, so nobody learns whether an id exists: the signature with the pool's access key and this check authorise a request, not the id, and the control plane decides it before any 409 or 410; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 no_gateway, a claim when the choice of the key's node pool resolves to no gateway, claim.schema.json, or a handover at which the node pool has no gateway the run could be registered through, for one of the causes handover.schema.json gives, after which the dispatch stays claimed until its lease lapses; 409 handed_over, a handover for a run that was handed over before, through this or any other dispatch, while the run goes on, since a run key is handed over at most once per run; 409 not_dispatched, a handover before dispatched; 409 not_prebuild, a prebuilt for a dispatch whose step is not prebuild; 409 not_handed_over, a prebuilt for a dispatch that was not handed over yet; 409 run_mismatch, a prebuilt whose run_id is not the dispatch's run; these three apply to prebuilt alone, prebuilt.schema.json; 409 lease_expired, a dispatched, a handover, a release or a prebuilt naming a stale dispatch, one whose lease lapsed before its handover, while its run has not ended, as handover.schema.json describes, on which the starter stops the job it started for that dispatch; 410 gone, a request naming a dispatch that ended: at its release before its handover, as release.schema.json describes, or at a handover whose run the control plane cannot form, for one of the causes handover.schema.json gives, which ends the run and the dispatch, in the same step, frees the slot the dispatch took, and answers that handover 410 gone, or when its work item was closed or undone while the dispatch was neither stale nor handed over, or with its run once stale, as handover.schema.json describes, or with its run after its handover, since closing or undoing the work item after the handover does not end the dispatch at once and the run goes on to its end, or after a prebuilt ended the dispatch, prebuilt.schema.json, a second prebuilt among them; a dispatch of the step prebuild has no work item, so the closing or undoing of a work item never ends it, and it ends only at a prebuilt, at a release, with its run, at the run's outcome or when the control plane finds the run lost, once handed over, and once stale, at a handover whose run the control plane cannot form, or when the collection whose target it is for is disconnected or ends, which ends the dispatch and its run with no new run; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the starter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry; 503 unavailable, a handover the control plane could not carry out because it failed to make the run's inputs or its run key, a failure a retry may clear, other than a run the control plane cannot form, which is 410 gone, decided after every other cause in the order handover.schema.json gives, which says when the starter sends it again. A release after its handover, while the run goes on, is not refused: it is answered as a success, the signed 204, and ends the run. A handover's refusals, and a release's, apply in the order handover.schema.json gives. A prebuilt's refusals apply in the order prebuilt.schema.json gives: 403 forbidden, 410 gone, 409 lease_expired, 409 not_prebuild, 409 not_handed_over, 409 run_mismatch. No refusal is tied to a policy, and one is tied to a step: 409 not_prebuild, which refuses a prebuilt for a dispatch whose step is not prebuild. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and the starter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the starter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the starter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A member this schema does not define is refused.
